newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ENDEMOL SHARE OFFERING PRICED AT NLG 48.00.
newsitem.headline: ENDEMOL SHARE OFFERING PRICED AT NLG 48.00.

text.p: Endemol Entertainment Holding NV's initial public offering was priced at 48.00 guilders per share, global co-ordinator ABN AMRO Bank NV said.

ABN AMRO said the size of the offering had been fixed at 9.69 million ordinary shares, which consisted of 4.40 million new common shares issued by the company and 5.29 million offered by shareholders Joop van den Ende and John de Mol.
The shares, which will have the Reuter Instrument Code (RIC) EMOL.AS, are due to start trading on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange on November 1.

ABN AMRO earlier said the shares would be offered at a price of between 44 and 48 guilders. The offering was first planned to close on November 6, but due to strong demand subscriptions closed on October 29 at 1400 GMT.
Dutch retail investors, and the Dutch and international institutional investors have each been allocated about one third of the total offered common shares, ABN AMRO said.

The selling shareholders had granted the global co-ordinator an option to purchase up to a maximum of 1.45 million additional common shares. The option can be exercised within a period of 30 days after the payment and delivery date, it added.
Endemol, is one of Europe's biggest television production companies, was formed in 1994 by a merger of the production companies of co-chairmen Van den Ende and De Mol.
Its net profit rose 38 percent to 60.5 million guilders in the financial year to July 31, 1996 on a turnover of 642.4 million guilders.
The company expects net profit to rise by 15 to 20 percent in the current 1996/97 financial year and predicts that both sales and profits will double within five years.
Endemol already generates some 40 percent of its turnover outside the Netherlands and plans further expansion abroad.
